lanes.title: the AutoResolver for every domain on battalions, its throughput, the parity bar, walls in both resolvers (D-087 DF6, D-088 DG12-DG13)
lanes.brief:
SCOPE LIMITS: as lane OC: prototypes/m7-sprint1 (M7Proto.slnx and its bench) and docs/m7-plan only; no Sim.* change, no permanent project, no CI change. PROPOSAL where the Director delegated; READING with both alternatives; nothing invented or reopened.

READ FIRST: D-087 (DF6; §4: lane D's READING A is superseded), D-088 (DG12; DG13 with DG13-R1 to DG13-R4; §3: lane MOR3's walls PROPOSAL is superseded), D-089 DH9 (DG13-R3 (a) and DG13-R4 (a) confirmed) and D-090 DI1; D-079 Q4, DIR5 §2.1 and §2.13; reports H-P (rule P1, battery P, its seeds), parity-report.md, E-autoresolve.md, H-D (ResolverPolicy, READING A), H-N (the TacticalResolver's naval, air, combined-arms and sniper model), H-RAM (ramming), H-S (sieges, walls and wall levels), H-MOR3 §13 (the walls observation), and H-OC and H-BN (the outcome rules and the battalion model you build on); code Proto.M7/Tactical (AutoResolver.cs, AutoAxis.cs, DomainProfiles.cs, DomainTypes.cs, ResolverPolicy.cs, ParityBatteryP.cs, ParityCriteriaP1.cs, ParityCalibrationP.cs, TacticalBattle.Domain*.cs, RamPhysics.cs), Proto.M7/War/Siege and Proto.M7.Bench.

(1) EVERY DOMAIN AUTO-RESOLVED (D-087 DF6). Extend the AutoResolver's model to aircraft, vessels, crew-served guns and embarked troops, on battalions (lane BN), so that no AI-vs-AI battle runs the TacticalResolver: for AI-vs-AI the default becomes the AutoResolver for every setup (ResolverPolicy; AutoUnsupportedReason retired for the domains now modelled), while a battle with a player still defaults to the TacticalResolver (DIR5 §2.1 and §2.13 unchanged). State the model's equations in the document, per domain and across domains (air against air and against ground or sea; naval engagement with ramming and boarding as the TacticalResolver models them; crew-served fire; embarkation and landing; combined arms): dt-correct, in integer or fixed-point arithmetic (never float), deterministic, with coefficients calibrated on the tuning seeds only. Lane OC's outcome rules (fighting is damage, the tie, the Standoff tie, one role per side) hold in the new domains as in land battles.

(2) THROUGHPUT (DF6's reason: 12 players and 40-50 air or naval battles between turns). A bench mode in Proto.M7.Bench that measures the AutoResolver's wall time per battle by domain and size (up to D-088 DG3's 5 battalions per side), and the total for the Director's figures, with the land battles of a busy turn stated as an assumption; Release, one thread and four threads, on this machine; the TacticalResolver run headless on the same setups for comparison. Report the numbers. Whether they fit a pause between turns is INFERRED; no budget is invented.

(3) PARITY (D-088 DG12, answering D-079 Q4). The bar: the AutoResolver picks the TacticalResolver's winner in at least 95% of the test battles, with casualties within about 15%; the Director asks for better accuracy than that where it can be had. Before any tuning, pre-commit in the document how this is measured, as a PROPOSAL with its alternatives: per scenario or pooled; 'casualties within about 15%' as each side's losses relative to the TacticalResolver's, with zero-loss sides and ties handled explicitly; ties (lane OC) are outcomes the AutoResolver must match. Run it on lane P's battery P (tuning seeds 1-80; acceptance seeds never used before; held-out scenarios), extended with the new domains (air, naval, crew-served, embarked, combined arms), with walled battles (item 4) and with lane OC's rewritten Ambush (now deployment-legal). Report per family and overall, before and after tuning, with the TacticalResolver against itself (seed halves) as the noise floor. Never loosen a band after seeing results. Push beyond the bar where the model allows, and say where it cannot and why.

(4) WALLS IN BOTH RESOLVERS (D-088 DG13; DG13-R1 (a), DG13-R2 (a), DG13-R3 (a), DG13-R4 (a)). Defenders fighting from walls fight as if their troops were tripled (archers quadrupled), in attack and in toughness; each improved wall level adds one more multiple (level 1: x3, archers x4; level 2: x4 and x5; level 3: x5 and x6). Walls add nothing against an attacker that fields artillery able to breach them, a capability computed from the attacker's battalions and research (Law 4: never a date or an era label). The TacticalResolver keeps the walls' geometry for movement. The multiplier is a term inside the resolution equations (Law 2), applied in both resolvers from lane S's siege model and wall levels. Tests in both resolvers, and walled scenarios in the parity battery.

(5) DOCUMENTS AND CHECKS. The AutoResolver's design in a document under docs/m7-plan (new, or an amended existing one; PROPOSAL where design; superseded statements struck in place with dated notes); a semantic test per domain and per mechanism; tie-dense tests for any ordering on double-valued scores; a populated-table round-trip test for every new or changed serialized row; bounded mutants with semantic kills; the determinism scan; the doc-link check.
